title: Overlap of Two Busy Calendars
statement:
Two people share their calendars as lists of busy blocks, a and b. Each block is [start, end] and includes both ends. Within one list the blocks are sorted by start and never overlap or touch each other.

Return every stretch of time when both people are busy, as a list of [start, end] blocks sorted by start. A single shared moment counts: if one block ends at 5 and another starts at 5, the answer contains [5, 5].

examples.why: [3, 9] overlaps both of a's blocks, so one block in b can produce several pieces of the answer.
Both ends are inclusive, so the single moment 5 is shared. A strict comparison would miss it.
If one calendar is empty, nobody is busy together.

constraints: Each list is sorted and its blocks are disjoint: a[i].end < a[i + 1].start
hints: Two blocks [s1, e1] and [s2, e2] share time exactly when max(s1, s2) ≤ min(e1, e2). What is the shared piece?
Both lists are sorted. Can you walk them together like the merge step of merge sort?
Keep an index into each list. Record the overlap of the two current blocks if there is one, then advance whichever block ends first: it cannot overlap anything later in the other list.

explain.intuition:
Two blocks overlap on [max(starts), min(ends)] when that range is not empty. The question is which pairs to test. Since both lists are sorted and disjoint, walk them with one pointer each, like merging two sorted arrays.

The key move: after checking the current pair, drop the block that ends first. Every later block in the other list starts after the current one in that list, so the block that ended first has nothing more to overlap. The block that ends later might still reach into the next block on the other side, so it stays. This is the same as finding when two people are both free or both busy in a scheduling UI.
steps: Set i = j = 0 and an empty result.
While both indexes are in range, let lo = max(a[i][0], b[j][0]) and hi = min(a[i][1], b[j][1]).
Return the result. It is already sorted, since each piece starts after the previous one ends.
pitfalls: Using lo < hi. The ends are inclusive, so a single shared point [5, 5] must be kept.
Advancing the block that starts first instead of the one that ends first. A long block like [3, 9] would be dropped while it still overlaps [8, 12].
Advancing both pointers after a match. One long block can overlap several blocks of the other list.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Test each block of a against each block of b and collect the overlaps, then sort them by start.

solutions.title: Two pointers, drop whichever ends first
solutions.idea: Walk both sorted lists together. Record the overlap of the current pair, then advance the block with the smaller end.

followups: Return the times when at least one of k people is free during working hours. What changes?
The calendars arrive as streams you can only read once. Does the two-pointer walk still work?
